title: Small coalitions can bias a monotone Boolean function
statement: Let $n\ge 2$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be monotone, with the signs ordered by $-1<1$. If the uniform mean of $f$ is at least $-99/100$, there is a set $J$ of coordinates such that forcing every coordinate in $J$ to $1$ gives a function with mean at least $99/100$, and $|J|\le 10000n/\log n$. If the mean of $f$ is at most $99/100$, there is a set $J$ such that forcing every coordinate in $J$ to $-1$ gives a function with mean at most $-99/100$, and $|J|\le 10000n/\log n$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a monotone function from the $n$ dimensional sign cube to $\{-1,1\}$
For the first conclusion, the mean of $f$ is at least $-99/100$
For the second conclusion, the mean of $f$ is at most $99/100$
